summary: Dimension on two parallel lines now gives the distance between them, as in CATIA, instead of failing because the lines are too close to parallel for an angle. Sketches gain a point-line-distance relation {id, kind: point-line-distance, pointId, lineId, value} that holds a point at a positive distance, a number or an expression, from the infinite support of a line, and reference dimensions gain the measurement {kind: point-line-distance, pointId, lineId}, which Make driving turns into the relation. The point keeps the side of the line it starts on through value edits, other solves and drags. For two parallel lines, Dimension stores the distance from an endpoint of the second line to the first line together with a Parallel relation, and commits the distance without the Parallel, still as one edit, when the solver finds the Parallel redundant; lines that are not parallel still take an angle. A point and a line, or an arc or circle and a line, picked in either order or selected together, take the distance from the point or the curve's center. Two arcs or circles take Center distance, a point with an arc or circle takes the point-pair distances to its center, and an arc or circle with the origin or an axis places its center. A picked arc or circle now waits for the next pick; picking it again or clicking empty space opens its size. The relation compiles to a new native signed point-to-line equation, so the native buffer protocol moves from 5 to 6 and the committed WebAssembly module is rebuilt. Split, Extend and the remaining pieces of a Trim keep the relation on the piece that keeps the line's identity, which stays on the same support; Trim lists it in removedRelationIds when it deletes the line or the point.
warning: Potentially breaking for CAD files: a document whose sketch contains a point-line-distance relation, or a reference dimension with a point-line-distance measurement, cannot be opened by release 0.0.775 or earlier, because their strict relation schema rejects the new kind. Existing documents are not migrated or rewritten; only sketches where a person or agent adds the relation carry it, and Dimension now adds it for two parallel lines, a point and a line, and an arc or circle and a line. Potentially breaking for automation that drives the Dimension pick flow: a picked arc or circle no longer opens its size at once; pick it again or click empty space. A selected arc or circle still opens its size directly. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output.

checklist.schema: CAD schema 2 sketch graphs gain the additive relation {id, kind: point-line-distance, pointId, lineId, value} and the reference-dimension measurement {kind: point-line-distance, pointId, lineId}. The strict relation union means release 0.0.775 and earlier reject a document that contains either. No migration and no change to existing relation kinds, UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal or worker reply. The native buffer protocol moves from 5 to 6: version 6 appends the point-line-distance equation kind and keeps every other code and the reply format. The Rust solver and committed WebAssembly module are rebuilt together with the app, and the 0.0.757 baseline comparison asks that module in its own protocol 5. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. When the solver rejects the Parallel added with a parallel-line distance only as redundant, Dimension leaves it out of the preview, or submits the distance alone once more with the same identities, signal and base version, and only one edit is accepted. WebMCP tools keep their arguments; set-sketch-relation accepts the new relation and reference measurement through the shared sketch schema, and the public agent guide describes both.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. In sketches, Dimension measures two parallel lines, a point or an arc or circle center from a line, two arc or circle centers, a point from an arc or circle center, and an arc or circle center from the origin or an axis.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage format change. Saved documents open unchanged; a document saved with the new relation needs this release or later.
checklist.verification: cadSketchPointLineDistanceRelations.test.ts checks parsing and rejection of the relation and reference measurement, the unsigned residual on either side, beyond the segment and far from the origin, invalid values and expressions, references and deletion protection, the parallel-line distance for exact, nearly parallel, tilted and collinear lines, reference measurement and Make driving, and Trim, Split and Extend keeping or removing the relation. cadSketchPointLineDistancePreparation.test.ts checks with the native solver that the relation removes one freedom and holds the point on its starting side through value and expression edits and drags across the line, for forward and reversed lines on both sides and far from the origin, that a reference measures without driving, and that a Parallel between two vertical lines is reported redundant while the distance alone holds and moves both. The Rust tests check the signed value and derivatives on either side, for a reversed line and far from the origin, a zero-length line, and a solve that holds a parallel line at a signed distance. nativeBaseline.test.ts asks the 0.0.757 module in its protocol 5, which rejects the new kind, and compares every corpus, seeded and benchmark call as before. CadSketchRelationsPanel.test.tsx checks the parallel-line distance with its Parallel and one Undo, the redundant Parallel left out after its preview and at Apply, the reference distance, the point, circle and center pairs and the endpoint error. CadWorkbench.test.tsx checks picks in both orders, selection, the toolbar and the context menu for parallel and slanted lines, a point and a line, a circle and a line, two circles, a point and a circle, and a circle and the origin or an axis, and an arc that waits for its second pick. cadSketchGraphDimensionLayout.test.ts checks the perpendicular annotation and its extension. The full Vitest suite (552 files, 6222 tests), lint, ui:check, build, solver:check (172 Rust tests; the module matches its source) and the release check pass, and e2e cad-sketch-constraints, cad-sketch-context-editing, cad-sketch-dimension-points, cad-sketch-mirror-copy, cad-sketch-reference-dimensions and cad-workflow pass in Chromium (63 tests).

publicNotes.summary: Dimension measures between parallel lines and from a point to a line.
changes: Dimension on two parallel lines gives the distance between them and keeps them parallel, instead of an angle error. Lines that another relation already keeps parallel get the distance alone.
Dimension on a point and a line gives the point's distance from the line, measured square to its full extension. The point stays on its side of the line while you edit or drag.

An arc or circle with a line measures from its center, two arcs or circles take Center distance, a point with an arc or circle measures to its center, and an arc or circle with the origin or an axis places its center.
A picked arc or circle now waits for a second pick. Pick it again or click empty space for its size.
publicNotes.compatibility: Sketches that use Point to line distance cannot be opened by release 0.0.775 or earlier. Existing documents are not changed. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: No action needed. Open sketches that use Point to line distance with this release or later. To size an arc or circle with Dimension, pick it twice or pick it and click empty space.
